L30: # Addendum to the article ‘Global pluripotential theory over a trivially valued field’
L31: 
L32: Sébastien Boucksom and Mattias Jonsson Address: CNRS–CMLS
L33: École Polytechnique
L34: F-91128 Palaiseau Cedex
L35: France Email address: sebastien.boucksom@polytechnique.edu Address: Dept of Mathematics
L36: University of Michigan
L37: Ann Arbor, MI 48109-1043
L38: USA Email address: mattiasj@umich.edu
L39: 
L40: Date: August 24, 2026
L41: ###### Abstract.
L42: This note is an addendum to the paper ‘Global pluripotential theory over a trivially valued field’ by the present authors, in which we prove two results. Let $X$ be an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed field field $k$, and assume that $k$ has characteristic zero, or that $X$ has dimension at most two. We first prove that when $X$ is smooth, the envelope property holds for any numerical class on $X$.
L43: Then we prove that for $X$ possibly singular and for an ample numerical class, the Monge–Ampère energy of a bounded function is equal to the energy of its usc regularized plurisubharmonic envelope.
L44: Cette note est un appendice au papier ‘Global pluripotential theory over a trivially valued field’ par les présents auteurs, dans lequel nous prouvons deux résultats. Soit $X$ une variété projective irreductible sur un corps algébriquement clos $k$, et supposons que $k$ est de caractéristique nulle, ou que $X$ est de dimension au plus deux. Nous prouvons d’abord que, lorsque $X$ est lisse, la propriété d’enveloppe est valable pour toute classe numérique sur $X$.
L45: Ensuite, nous prouvons que, pour $X$ possiblement singulier et pour toute classe numérique ample, l’énergie de Monge–Ampère de toute fonction bornée est égale à celle de son enveloppe plurisousharmonique regularisée.
L46: ## Introduction
L47: 
L48: The purpose of this note is to strengthen two results in the article [【17†BJ22a】], where we developed global pluripotential on the Berkovich analytification over a trivially valued field. The results here are used in [【18†BJ22b】, 【19†BJ22c】]. One should view the current note as an addendum to [【17†BJ22a】], rather than a stand-alone paper.
L49: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and $X$ an irreducible projective variety over $k$. To any numerical class $\theta\in\Num(X)$ we associate a class $\PSH(\theta)$ of $\theta$-psh functions; these are upper semicontinuous functions $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ on the Berkovich analytification of $X$ with respect to the trivial absolute value on $k$.
L50: We say that $\theta$ has the envelope property if for any bounded-above family $(\varphi_{\alpha})_{\alpha}$ in $\PSH(\theta)$, the function $\sup^{\star}_{\alpha}\varphi_{\alpha}$ is $\theta$-psh.
L51: ###### Theorem A.
L52: 
L53: Assume that $X$ is smooth, and that $\charac k=0$ or $\dim X\leq 2$. Then any numerical class $\theta\in\Num(X)$ has the envelope property.
L54: 
L55: In [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 5.20], this was established for nef classes $\theta$ following [【20†BFJ16】], and the proof here is not so different.
L56: For the second result we allow $X$ to be singular, but work with an ample class $\omega\in\Num(X)$. The $\omega$-psh envelope $\env_{\omega}(\varphi)$ of a bounded function $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}$ is defined as the supremum of all functions $\psi\in\PSH(\omega)$ with $\psi\leq\varphi$, and the envelope property for $\omega$ is equivalent to continuity of envelopes in the sense of $\env_{\omega}(\varphi)$ being continuous whenever $\varphi$ is continuous.
L57: It is also equivalent to the usc envelope $\env_{\omega}^{\star}(\varphi)$ being $\omega$-psh for any bounded function $\varphi$.
L58: In [【17†BJ22a】] we also defined the Monge–Ampère energy $\en_{\omega}(\varphi)\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ of any bounded-above function $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$. We did this first for $\omega$-psh functions in terms of an energy pairing ultimately deriving from intersection numbers on compactified test configurations, see §【10†1.4】 below, then for general bounded-above functions $\varphi$, setting
L59:  | $$\en_{\omega}(\varphi):=\sup\{\en_{\omega}(\psi)\mid\psi\in\PSH(\omega),\psi\leq\varphi\}.$$  |
L60: We say that $(X,\omega)$ satisfies the weak envelope property if there exists a projective birational morphism $\pi\colon\tilde{X}\to X$ and an ample class $\tilde{\omega}\in\Num(\tilde{X})$ such that $(\tilde{X},\tilde{\omega})$ has the envelope property and $\tilde{\omega}\geq\pi^{\star}\omega$ (by which we mean $\tilde{\omega}-\pi^{\star}\omega$ is nef). It follows from [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 5.20] that the weak envelope property holds when $\charac k=0$ or $\dim X\leq 2$.
L61: ###### Theorem B.
L62: 
L63: Assume that $\omega\in\Num(X)$ is an ample class, and that the weak envelope property holds for $(X,\omega)$. Then, for any bounded function $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}$, we have
L64: 
L65:  | $$\en_{\omega}(\varphi)=\en_{\omega}(\env_{\omega}(\varphi))=\en_{\omega}(\env_{\omega}^{\star}(\varphi)).$$  |
L66: The first equality is definitional, see [【17†BJ22a】, (8.2)], and the second equality follows from [【17†BJ22a】, Proposition 8.3] if $\omega$ has the envelope property. The main content of Theorem B is thus the second equality when the envelope property is unknown or even fails (for example, when $X$ is not unibranch).

L71: ## 1. Preliminaries
L72: 
L73: Throughout the paper, $X$ is an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed field $k$.
L74: ### 1.1. The $\theta$-psh envelope
L75: 
L76: Fix any numerical class $\theta\in\Num(X)$. We refer to [【17†BJ22a】, §4] for the definition of the class $\PSH(\theta)$ of $\theta$-psh functions. We have that $\PSH(\theta)$ is nonempty only if $\theta$ is psef, whereas $\PSH(\theta)$ contains the constant functions iff $\theta$ is nef.
L77: ###### Definition 1.1.
L78: 
L79: The $\theta$-psh envelope of a function $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{\pm\infty\}$ is the function $\env_{\theta}(\varphi)\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{\pm\infty\}$ defined as the pointwise supremum
L80: 
L81:  | $$\env_{\theta}(\varphi):=\sup\left\{\psi\in\PSH(\theta)\mid\psi\leq\varphi\right\}.$$  |
L82: Thus $\env_{\theta}(\varphi)\equiv-\infty$ iff there is no $\psi\in\PSH(\theta)$ with $\psi\leq\varphi$. When $\theta=c_{1}(L)$ for a $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $L$, we write $\pp_{L}:=\pp_{\theta}$. Despite the name, $\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$ is not always $\theta$-psh (and indeed not even usc in general). However, it is clear that
L83: 
L84:   * •
L85: 
L86: $\varphi\mapsto\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$ is increasing;
L87: 
L88:   * •
L89: 
L90: $\env_{\theta}(\varphi+c)=\env_{\theta}(\varphi)+c$ for all $c\in\mathbb{R}$.
L91: The envelope operator is also continuous along increasing nets of lsc functions:
L92: ###### Lemma 1.2.
L93: 
L94: If $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ is the pointwise limit of an increasing net $(\varphi_{j})$ of bounded-below, lsc functions, then $\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})\nearrow\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$ pointwise on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$.
L95: ###### Proof.
L96: We trivially have $\lim_{j}\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})=\sup_{j}\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})\leq\env_{\theta}(\varphi)$. Pick $\varepsilon>0$ and $\psi\in\PSH(\theta)$ such that $\psi\leq\varphi$, and hence $\psi<\varphi+\varepsilon$. Since $\psi$ is usc and the $\varphi_{j}$ is lsc, a simple variant of Dini’s lemma shows that $\psi<\varphi_{j}+\varepsilon$ for all $j$ large enough, and hence $\psi\leq\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})+\varepsilon$.
L97: Taking the supremum over $\psi$ yields $\env_{\theta}(\varphi)\leq\sup_{j}\env_{\theta}(\varphi_{j})$, and we are done. ∎
L98: As in [【21†BE21】, Lemma 7.30], the envelope property admits the following useful reformulation.
L99: ###### Lemma 1.3.
L100: 
L101: If $\PSH(\theta)\neq\emptyset$, then the following statements are equivalent:
L102: 
L103:   * (i)
L104: 
L105: $\theta$ has the envelope property;
L106: 
L107:   * (ii)
L108: 
L109: for any function $\varphi\colon X^{\mathrm{an}}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{\pm\infty\}$, we have
L110: 
L111:  | $$\env_{\theta}(\varphi)\equiv-\infty,\,\env_{\theta}(\varphi)^{\star}\equiv+\infty,\text{ or }\env_{\theta}(\varphi)^{\star}\in\PSH(\theta);$$  |
L112: 
L113:   * (iii)

L269: ### 2.2. Consequences
L270: 
L271: We now list some consequences of Theorem A. First, we can characterize psef classes, similarly to the complex analytic case.
L272: 
L273: ###### Corollary 2.1.
L274: 
L275: Assume that $X$ satisfies the assumptions in Theorem A. Then, for any $\theta\in\Num(X)$, we have $\PSH(\theta)\neq\emptyset$ iff $\theta$ is psef. Moreover, in this case, the function
L276: 
L277:  | $$V_{\theta}:=\pp_{\theta}(0)$$  |
L278: 
L279: is $\theta$-psh.
L280: ###### Proof.
L281: 
L282: It follows from [【17†BJ22a】, Definition 4.1] that $\PSH(\theta)\neq\emptyset$ only if $\theta$ is psef. First suppose $\theta$ is big. By Theorem A, $V_{\theta}:=\pp_{\theta}(0)$ is $\theta$-psh. Note that $V_{\theta}(v_{\mathrm{triv}})=\sup V_{\theta}=0$, where $v_{\mathrm{triv}}$ is the trivial valuation on $X$.
L283: Now suppose $\theta$ is merely psef, and pick a sequence $(\theta_{m})_{1}^{\infty}$ of big classes converging to $\theta$, such that $\theta\leq\theta_{m+1}\leq\theta_{m}$ for all $m$. As $\PSH(\theta_{m+1})\subset\PSH(\theta_{m})$ for all $m$, the sequence $(V_{\theta_{m}})_{m}$ is pointwise decreasing on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$. Let $\varphi$ be its limit. We have $\sup\varphi=\varphi(v_{\mathrm{triv}})=0$, and $\varphi\in\PSH(\theta_{m})$ for every $m$.
L284: It now follows from [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 4.5] that $\varphi\in\PSH(\theta)$. Finally, it is easy to see that $\varphi=\pp_{\theta}(0)$. Indeed, $\varphi\leq 0$, and if $\psi\in\PSH(\theta)$ satisfies $\psi\leq 0$, then $\psi\in\PSH(\theta_{m})$ for all $m$, so $\psi\leq V_{\theta_{m}}$, and hence $\psi\leq\varphi$. ∎
L285: By [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 5.11], Theorem A now implies the following compactness result.
L286: ###### Corollary 2.2.
L287: 
L288: Under the assumptions on $X$ of Theorem A, the set
L289: 
L290:  | $$\PSH_{\sup}(\theta)=\left\{\varphi\in\PSH(\theta)\mid\sup\varphi=0\right\}$$  |
L291: 
L292: is compact for any psef class $\theta\in\Num(X)$.
L293: 
L294: Finally, as an immediate consequence of Theorem A and [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 6.31], we have the following version of Siu’s decomposition theorem.
L295: ###### Corollary 2.3.
L296: 
L297: Suppose that $X$ satisfies the assumptions of Theorem A. Pick $\theta\in\Num(X)$ and an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor $E$. Then, for any $\varphi\in\PSH(\theta)$, we have:
L298: 
L299:  | $$\varphi\leq\log|s_{E}|+O(1)\Longleftrightarrow\varphi-\log|s_{E}|\in\PSH(\theta-E).$$  |
L300: 
L301: As before, $\log|s_{E}|=m^{-1}\log|s_{mE}|$, where $s_{mE}$ is the canonical global section of $\mathcal{O}_{X}(mE)$ for any $m\geq 1$ such that $mE$ is integral.
L302: ## 3. Proof of Theorem B
L303: 
L304: We start by proving:
L305: 
L306: ###### Lemma 3.1.
L307: 
L308: Let $\pi\colon\tilde{X}\to X$ be a projective birational morphism, and pick a bounded $\omega$-psh function $\psi$. Then $(\omega,\psi)^{n+1}=(\pi^{\star}\omega,\pi^{\star}\psi)^{n+1}$.
L309: 
L310: Here $\pi^{\star}\omega$ may not be ample, but the right hand side is well-defined, as $\pi^{\star}\psi$ is a function of finite energy. In fact $\pi^{\star}\psi\in\mathcal{E}^{1}(\tilde{\omega})$ for any ample class $\tilde{\omega}\geq\pi^{\star}\omega$.
L311: ###### Proof.
L312: The case when $\psi\in\PL(X)$ follows from Lemma 【31†1.8】. In the general case, write $\psi$ as the pointwise limit of a decreasing net $(\psi_{j})$ in $\PL\cap\PSH(\omega)$, and pick $\tilde{\omega}\in\Amp(\tilde{X})$ such that $\tilde{\omega}\geq\pi^{\star}\omega$. Then $\pi^{\star}\psi_{j}$ decreases to $\pi^{\star}\psi$ pointwise on $\tilde{X}^{\mathrm{an}}$.
L313: Moreover, $\pi^{\star}\psi_{j}$ and $\pi^{\star}\psi$ are $\tilde{\omega}$-psh, and hence lie in $\mathcal{E}^{1}(\tilde{\omega})$ as they are bounded. By [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 7.14 (iii)] we have $(\omega,\psi_{j})^{n+1}\to(\omega,\psi)^{n+1}$ and $(\pi^{\star}\omega,\pi^{\star}\psi_{j})^{n+1}\to(\pi^{\star}\omega,\pi^{\star}\psi)^{n+1}$. Now $(\pi^{\star}\omega,\pi^{\star}\psi_{j})^{n+1}=(\omega,\psi_{j})^{n+1}$ for all $j$ by the PL case, and the result follows. ∎
L314: As stated in the introduction, we introduce:
L315: ###### Definition 3.2.
L316: 
L317: Let $X$ be a projective variety, and $\omega\in\Num(X)$ an ample class. We say that $(X,\omega)$ has the weak envelope property if there exists a projective birational morphism $\pi\colon\tilde{X}\to X$, and an ample class $\tilde{\omega}\in\Num(\tilde{X})$, such that $\tilde{\omega}\geq\pi^{\star}\omega$ and $(\tilde{X},\tilde{\omega})$ has the envelope property.
L318: ###### Lemma 3.3.
L319: 
L320: If $\charac k=0$ or $\dim X\leq 2$, then any ample class $\omega\in\Num(X)$ has the weak envelope property.
L321: 
L322: ###### Proof.
L323: 
L324: In both cases, we can pick $\pi\colon\tilde{X}\to X$ as a resolution of singularities, and then pick any ample class $\tilde{\omega}\geq\pi^{\star}\omega$. By [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 5.20] (or Theorem A), the envelope property holds for $(\tilde{X},\tilde{\omega})$, and we are done. ∎
L325: ###### Proof of Theorem B.
L326: Set $\tau:=\env_{\omega}(\varphi)$. For any $\psi\in\PSH(\omega)$, we have $\psi\leq\varphi\Longleftrightarrow\psi\leq\tau$, and hence $\en_{\omega}(\varphi)=\en_{\omega}(\tau)\leq\en_{\omega}(\tau^{\star})$. Since $\tau$ is the pointwise supremum of the family $\mathcal{F}=\{\psi\in\PSH(\omega)\mid\psi\leq\varphi\}$, and since $\mathcal{F}$ is stable under finite max, we can find an increasing net $(\psi_{i})$ of $\omega$-psh functions such that $\sup_{i}\psi_{i}=\tau$ pointwise on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$.
L327: Replacing $\psi_{i}$ with $\max\{\psi_{i},\inf\psi\}$, we can further assume that $\psi_{i}$ is bounded.
L328: By assumption, we can find a projective birational morphism $\pi\colon\tilde{X}\to X$, and an ample class $\tilde{\omega}\in\Num(\tilde{X})$ such that $\tilde{\omega}\geq\pi^{\star}\omega$ and $(\tilde{X},\tilde{\omega})$ has the envelope property.
L329: Now $\tilde{\tau}:=\pi^{\star}\tau=\sup_{i}\pi^{\star}\psi_{i}$ with $\pi^{\star}\psi_{i}\in\PSH(\tilde{\omega})$, and it follows that $\tilde{\tau}^{\star}$ is $\tilde{\omega}$-psh, and coincides with $\tilde{\tau}=\sup_{i}\pi^{\star}\psi_{i}=\lim_{i}\sup\pi^{\star}\psi_{i}$ on $\tilde{X}^{\mathrm{div}}$. By [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 7.38], we get $(\pi^{\star}\omega,\pi^{\star}\psi_{i})^{n+1}\to(\pi^{\star}\omega,\tilde{\tau}^{\star})^{n+1}$. On the other hand, Lemma 【32†3.1】 yields
L330:  | $$(\pi^{\star}\omega,\pi^{\star}\psi_{i})^{n+1}=(\omega,\psi_{i})^{n+1}=(n+1)\vol(\omega)\en_{\omega}(\psi_{i})\leq(n+1)\vol(\omega)\en_{\omega}(\tau),$$  |
L331: 
L332: and we infer
L333: 
L334: (3.1)  |  | $$(\pi^{\star}\omega,\tilde{\tau}^{\star})^{n+1}\leq(n+1)\vol(\omega)\en_{\omega}(\tau).$$  |
L335: By [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 5.6] we also have $\tau^{\star}=\tau$ on $X^{\mathrm{div}}$. Each $\psi\in\PSH(\omega)$ such that $\psi\leq\tau^{\star}$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ therefore satisfies $\psi\leq\tau$ on $X^{\mathrm{div}}$ (see [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 5.6]); hence $\pi^{\star}\psi\leq\tilde{\tau}\leq\tilde{\tau}^{\star}$ on $\tilde{X}^{\mathrm{div}}$, which implies $\pi^{\star}\psi\leq\tilde{\tau}^{\star}$ on $\tilde{X}^{\mathrm{an}}$ (see [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 4.22]). Assuming $\psi$ bounded, we get
L336:  | $$(\omega,\psi)^{n+1}=(\pi^{\star}\omega,\pi^{\star}\psi)^{n+1}\leq(\pi^{\star}\omega,\tilde{\tau}^{\star})^{n+1},$$  |
L337: 
L338: where the equality follows from Lemma 【32†3.1】, and the inequality from the monotonicity of the energy pairing, see [【17†BJ22a】, Theorem 7.1]. Taking the supremum over $\psi$ now yields
L339: 
L340:  | $$(n+1)\vol(\omega)\en_{\omega}(\tau^{\star})\leq(\pi^{\star}\omega,\tilde{\tau}^{\star})^{n+1}.$$  |
L341: Combined with (【33†3.1】), this implies $\en_{\omega}(\tau^{\star})\leq\en_{\omega}(\tau)$, and the result follows. ∎
